status_summary: In December 2025 the Secretary of War issued a directive on the Chaplain Corps that eliminated the Army spiritual fitness guide effective 2025-12-16, began streamlining the faith coding system and described chaplains as moral anchors rather than emotional support, according to a Center Square report; the Justice Department welcomed the action on 2025-12-17. H.R. 8769, the Military Chaplains Modernization Act of 2026, was introduced on 2026-05-12 and referred to the House Armed Services Committee, its only action, and the identical Senate bill S. 5255 was introduced on 2026-08-05 and referred to the Senate Armed Services Committee; both would rewrite the chaplain sections of title 10 to set chaplain duties, protect ministry according to the chaplain's beliefs, bar retaliatory personnel actions and make violations punishable under the Uniform Code of Military Justice. The House sponsor filed the bill's text as an amendment to the FY2027 NDAA text with the House Rules Committee (dated 2026-06-12), and the Senate sponsor's release says it is included in the House-passed FY2027 NDAA, which was not confirmed from a primary source. No statute, directive or confirmation requirement using the Mandate's senior-officer readiness language was found, and neither bill contains such language.

timeline.event: A Secretary of War directive on the Chaplain Corps took effect, eliminating the Army spiritual fitness guide and streamlining faith and belief coding (date inferred from a report of 2025-12-18 saying the guide's elimination was effective Tuesday).
H.R. 8769, the Military Chaplains Modernization Act of 2026, was introduced and referred to the House Armed Services Committee.
S. 5255, the Senate Military Chaplains Modernization Act of 2026 (identical to H.R. 8769), was introduced and referred to the Senate Committee on Armed Services.

title: Protect chaplains' ministry and codify senior officers' readiness duty
uncertainties: The December 2025 directive was not read; its content comes from a Center Square report, and the Justice Department statement does not describe its provisions. The effective date 2025-12-16 is inferred from 'effective Tuesday' in a report dated Thursday 2025-12-18. A March 2026 report on a further chaplain memo (removing visible rank insignia, cutting faith codes) came from an aggregator and was dropped pending a reputable source. The texts of H.R. 8769 and S. 5255 and the House bill status (only action: referral on 2026-05-12, with S. 5255 listed as identical) were read on GovInfo; the Senate release is dated 2026-08-06, one day after the GovInfo introduction date. An NDAA amendment carrying the bill's text, offered by the House sponsor to Rules Committee Print 119-33, was found on the House Rules Committee amendment site, but whether it was made in order or adopted, and whether the House-passed FY2027 NDAA includes the text, was not verified. S. 5255 would also repeal subsection (b) of section 533 of the FY2013 NDAA, the existing chaplain conscience provision, and the old and new protections were not compared. Whether the executive chaplain changes strengthen or reduce chaplain protections is characterized differently by supporters and critics; the record treats them as a parallel match. The senior-officer duty language was searched (the 2025-09-30 Quantico address and confirmation hearings) with no qualifying codification. The FY2026 NDAA was checked only through its table of contents (Sec. 504 on chaplain career flexibility).
